Once you discover Jungle Body, there is no way back! Every class hypes you up and recharges your energy in a way that not many things can. Yin and all the JB babes know how to bring a good and effective workout that makes you sweat a lot, but feels like clubbing because everything happens in a room with nightclub lighting. We are always moving through the music, and sometimes the classes are with a live DJ as well, so it’s even more like a party.

The music is always the best, a bit of everything in every class. Attending classes actually expanded my music taste a lot because they really play a wide variety of styles. They also include dance steps from many different dance styles and mix them with boxing, cardio, and workout exercises, always following the music and having the best time—connecting with each other, laughing, and moving nonstop for 45 minutes. (Bring a towel couse you will sweat) Every week there are new routines and new dance steps to so you never get bored and it’s always a challenge.

I’d also like to mention something that I think kind of differentiates Jungle Body from other fitness groups or dance classes: every class has a different dress code, so we can all match! I don’t know, I feel like when we are all matching, the vibe, it’s different haha.

The vibe you’ll find is very high energy, mainly women, and very diverse. there are always people from everywhere. I’m personally from Chile, and I always find someone new to speak Spanish with in class haha. Yin, the main instructor, has an Asian background. I remember Pam is from the Philippines, Marion is from France, and all the backgrounds you can think about. There isn’t really an age range either; there are people of all ages. Some could be my granny, and sometimes kids come when Mimi, Yin’s wonderful, energetic, fun, talented, high-presence daughter comes and sometimes invites friends. So yeah anyone is welcome in class.

If you’re thinking of joining, don’t think twice because the first class is free—that’s how I started. I was just where the class was because I was taking a dance class before, and the energy of the people arriving caught my attention from a distance. I couldn’t resist going to ask what was going on that people were so excited about, and yeah… it makes sense that it was this.

I’m so grateful to Yin and all the Jungle Body team for making me feel welcome when I was new in Australia. They became my safe space and support system naturally and very quickly when I had no one else. It’s very special how no one goes unnoticed. It’s not like other dance or fitness classes where you pay, take the choreo or do the workout, everyone minds their own business, and leaves. Here, there is a lot of chatting, or even when there’s no time to talk because you’re dancing and moving, you exchange smiles with more than one person in the room and hear a few “hey,” “let’s go,” “c’mon,” “get it girl,” and lots of yells and screams hyping everyone up, coming from any of the JB babes who are always at the front keeping the energy high.

I’m so proud of what Jungle Body is now and what it’s becoming, because like everything, at first it was just a dream—Yin’s dream. Now it’s more than someone’s dream come true; and the proof that when you commit to something and put your whole heart in it, big things happen, and now JB it’s something meaningful and important for a lot of people. Always grateful to the universe for putting Jungle Body on my path. If you have the opportunity to join, please do—thank me later.

After sustaining a neck injury under his supervision, I was left alone while he went to get breakfast. Despite reporting symptoms like loss of feeling and grip strength, his response focused on terms and conditions instead of offering genuine support.

After wasting my time for over a week in deflective behaviours, he admitted that he lacked proper public liability and business insurance, stating, “I took a risk.” While he has boxing insurance, I sincerely hope it adequately covers the children and adolescents who make up most of his clients.

The owner’s approach to injury management, ethical responsibilities, and customer complaints was dismissive, defensive, and self-serving. When I raised concerns, I experienced deflection, gaslighting, and even unfounded legal threats that seemed aimed at intimidating, bullying, and silencing me.

Classes were frequently cancelled with little notice, started late, and often favoured specific clients rather than providing a structured experience for all. Refunds were never issued for cancelled classes, showing disregard for clients’ time and money.

This gym lacks professionalism and accountability, and the owner's behaviour creates an unsafe environment. If you choose to attend, I strongly recommend checking everything thoroughly, keeping clear records, and advocating for your rights.

My feedback aimed to improve safety standards, but it was ignored, the owner’s choice to ‘take a risk’ leaves me financially burdened and I have been treated incredibly poorly despite having been supportive and overly flexible with the owner and ‘head coach’.

When I went to the bike, the instructor (who is also the owner, Tanya Weeks) came over and told me it wasn’t my place. I tried to explain, but she went to the receptionist to check my number. The receptionist couldn’t find me in the system and didn’t even consider that there might have been a mistake or a system issue.

Instead, Tanya spoke to me in a rude manner, saying that I couldn’t just sit wherever I wanted and had to follow the allocation. I explained again that I had been assigned bike 23, but she was dismissive and moved me to a much worse spot — an older, wobbly bike at the end of the row.

The session itself was quite intense, and I had to ask multiple times for the fan to be turned on. It was only switched on later, and even then, with visible attitude.

No one apologised for the situation. I left feeling frustrated, uncomfortable, and frankly humiliated.

To be fair, other instructors are lovely — especially Hannah, Fede and Elena. If you decide to go, I would recommend booking with them.

However, based on this experience, I would not recommend attending classes with Tanya Weeks.

For context, we do have very strict arrival policies for all first-time riders due to the safety requirements involved with bike setup, cleat assistance, studio orientation, and induction before the class begins. Arriving exactly at class start unfortunately does not allow enough time for this process, especially in a full class environment. Arriving 5 minutes before the start of a class is already too late, all our policies and procedures on all of our touch points leading up to the class from the website, booking confirmation and  reservation reminders have a clear directive to arrive 15mins prior to the start time for first time guests. 

Our coaches are also responsible for maintaining the experience and focus of the room for all riders. During this particular class, there were multiple moments of loud talking and laughing throughout the session which became disruptive for both the coach and the 36 other riders in attendance. The coach addressed this in an effort to restore focus and flow for the rest of the class.

That said, we never want a guest to leave feeling uncomfortable, and we appreciate you taking the time to share your perspective. Our classes are high-energy and immersive, but they also rely heavily on respect for the coach, the experience, and the riders around you.

We wish you and your friends all the best in finding a studio environment better suited to what you’re looking for.
